Independent Co-ed Senior Day School London
World Ready
At Kew House, education is about preparing young people for what comes next. Through ambitious academics, enriching experiences and our value of ambition, originality, adaptability, curiosity and contribution, pupils develop knowledge, confidence and human skills to shape their own futures and make a difference.
Attend Our Open Event
Outstanding Achievement
With impressive GCSE and A Level results alongside exciting university destinations. From exceptional individual performances to places at leading universities, our Year 11 and Year 13 pupils demonstrated the ambition, curiosity and adaptability at the heart of a Kew House education.
Discover their achievements and see where our World-Ready pupils are heading next.
Our Values
The values that make pupils World-Ready.
At Kew House, academic achievement and personal development are inseparable. Ambition drives our pupils forward, while Originality, Adaptability and Curiosity shape how they think, learn and respond to the world around them.
Ultimately, we want them to use what they have learned to make a meaningful Contribution – to their school, their communities and the wider world. These values are not simply words. They are woven through our curriculum, enrichment and everyday school life, preparing pupils with the knowledge, confidence and human skills to be truly World-Ready.
The starting point.We encourage every pupil to aim high, challenge themselves and discover what they are capable of achieving.
Think independently. We give pupils the confidence to develop their own ideas, express their individuality and create solutions that are genuinely their own.
Ready for change.Pupils learn to think flexibly, respond to feedback, solve problems and approach unfamiliar situations with confidence.
Keep asking what next.We encourage pupils to question, explore and look beyond the obvious – developing an appetite for learning that reaches far beyond the classroom.
Make a difference.We encourage pupils to use their knowledge, talents and character to contribute positively to their school, their communities and the world beyond.

About Kew House School
An innovative, creative and welcoming west London Independent co-ed day school for 11-18 year olds.
Part of the family-owned Gardener Schools Group which includes Ravenscourt Park Prep School, Kew Green Prep School and Maida Vale School. Together they share knowledge, resources, contacts and a passion for education.
Kew House School is a warm and supportive community combining innovative teaching with state-of-the-art-facilities. They are ambitions for their students but are a greenhouse not a hothouse believing children fulfil their potential, personally and academically, when nurtured and inspired. They operate an ‘Open Door’ policy believing a child’s education is a shared responsibility, one that works best when all parties are engaged – school, parents and the students themselves.
Entry is at Y7 or Y12 and admission is based on exams and interviews. Kew House selects interesting, able and engaging students who will work together as a team supporting and inspiring one another. Why not join one of our next open mornings to find out how we can make a difference for your child. To read more click here for Headmaster’s Welcome

Headmaster’s Welcome
It is my privilege to walk amongst our learning community each day. Our pupils learn within a purposeful, inclusive and forgiving environment. The calmness of the atmosphere is the outcome of many simple features within the planning and running of the school. Pupils only ever move from a lesson to a break, rather than a lesson to a lesson. They solely carry the things they need with them for each lesson, not overburdened by hefty bags. The community runs on expectations not rules. Each year the Pupil Council review their expectations of each other, tweaking them as they feel appropriate.
The school celebrates achievement in all areas of pupil activity. Often ignored as an important element of inclusion, it is the recognition and respect that young people give to each other for their individual endeavors that bonds them as a group. From Oxbridge entry, to work experience with Formula 1 teams, Spotify streams to stage success, rowing medals to netball cups: our community cherishes and celebrates them all.
Pupils at Kew House are encouraged to face success and failure and ask themselves “what am I going to do differently next time?”. Building resilience is a vital component of senior school education and such reflective questioning is facilitated by outstanding pastoral care, aided by frequent reporting. Our pupils join Personal Tutor (PT) groups, vertically structured with members of each year group from Year 7 to Year 11. PTs meet daily and engage in peer-to-peer support as well as taking time to reflect on world events and their own progress.
By reporting once a month to pupils on their class progress, we give our pupils frequent updates on their progress, whilst providing the answer to the fundamental parental question “how are they doing?”. It is by working with our young people to help them to find their answers to their own improvement, be it academic, sporting, creative, friendships etc., that builds their confidence as they tackle evermore difficult life and school challenges. By individualising progress reporting to the statistical expectations of young people, we demonstrate the most important aspect of a Kew House education; “We are all individuals and that is what makes us all the same.”
We are a thriving school that, though tranquil in atmosphere, is buzzing with life. Our pupils, parents and in particular our excellent teaching staff work together to ensure that each day at school is a great day.
Will Williams Headmaster

Exclusive Partnership with Trailfinders
Exclusive Partnership with Trailfinders
Kew House School Sport finds a new home at Trailfinders Sports Club. A new era of sporting excellence begins in September 2025.
Kew House School is thrilled to announce a transformative development for our sports programme: as of September 2025, we will proudly become the exclusive school partner of Trailfinders Sports Club, located in the heart of Ealing. This exciting partnership marks a significant leap forward in delivering first-class sports facilities and opportunities for our pupils.
For years, Kew House School has fostered excellence across all domains of pupil life—from academics and the arts to music, drama and of course, sport. Our commitment to holistic education has always recognised that sports and physical activity play a vital role in developing character, confidence and community spirit. With this landmark move, Kew House School Sport is set to flourish like never before.
State-of-the-Art Sports Facilities for Our Pupils
Trailfinders Sports Club is one of London’s premier sports venues. Now, it becomes the official sporting home of Kew House School. Pupils will benefit from a range of cutting-edge sports facilities, including:
These facilities create an unparalleled environment for our pupils to engage in a wide variety of team and individual sports. Whether it’s rugby, football, hockey, netball, tennis or cricket, all sporting activities will now take place on one expansive, professionally managed campus.
A Hub for Physical and Mental Wellbeing
At Kew House School, sport is not just about competition—it is about building resilience, fostering teamwork, and supporting wellbeing. Our move to Trailfinders Sports Club reflects a deep commitment to this vision. The new facilities will not only allow pupils to strive for sporting excellence but will also provide a safe, energising and inclusive environment for every level of athletic ability.
This new sports hub aligns perfectly with our school’s ethos of holistic development. It offers opportunities for growth both on and off the pitch, helping pupils to develop life skills such as perseverance, leadership, collaboration and self-confidence.
A Social and Community-Focused Sporting Experience
Trailfinders Sports Club offers more than just pitches and courts. It is also a vibrant social venue with facilities for post-match gatherings, award ceremonies, and school community events. We are excited about the chance to bring our pupils, parents and staff together to celebrate our sporting achievements in such an inspiring setting.
By creating space for the social aspect of sport, we nurture the sense of community that makes Kew House School so special. We look forward to hosting a wide range of school sports events at Trailfinders, offering memorable experiences for everyone involved.
Continuing Strategic Investment in Sport
The move to Trailfinders Sports Club is the latest step in a wider strategy by the Gardener Schools Group to provide exceptional sporting opportunities for all pupils. Following the 2023 construction of the state-of-the-art Pier House fitness suite, this new partnership reflects a long-term vision of excellence in sport and wellbeing.
Our collaboration with Quinton Boat Club remains strong, with Kew House pupils continuing to benefit from the club’s newly rebuilt rowing facilities. In addition, our links with Brentford Football Club remain an important part of our wider community partnerships. Together, these collaborations highlight our commitment to giving pupils access to elite sports environments while staying rooted in local, community-focused values.
Partnerships That Go Beyond Sport
Our relationship with Trailfinders Sports Club is about more than just games and competitions. It’s about helping our pupils understand the lifelong value of physical activity. From health and fitness to teamwork and discipline, this partnership will support young people in becoming resilient, balanced and confident individuals.
This is part of our broader mission at Kew House School—to develop well-rounded pupils who thrive in all aspects of life. The role of sport in this journey is central, and Trailfinders will now play a key part in helping us deliver that promise.
Join Us in Celebrating the Future of Kew House School Sport
We look forward to welcoming parents, pupils and friends of Kew House School to Trailfinders in September 2025. Together, we will celebrate sport, achievement and the community spirit that lies at the heart of everything we do.
This is more than a change of venue—this is a bold investment in our future. We invite you to be part of it. As we step onto the pitches and courts of Trailfinders Sports Club, we do so with pride, ambition and a renewed commitment to excellence in everything we do.

Drama
We must all do theatre, to find out who we are and discover who we could become – Augusto Baol (Brazilian Drama Theorist, Founder of Theatre of the Oppressed)
At Kew House School, opportunities to participate in drama are woven into the curriculum. We believe that taking part in a dramatic production of any kind is an incredibly valuable way to learn many important skills needed throughout life; Drama encourages creativity and imagination, it encourages students to think outside the box and take risks. It is a collaborative artform that helps students to develop empathy and to better understand others, by seeing how the world looks through another person’s eyes. Communication and literacy skills are also enhanced, and we see a great many of our students develop and improve their presentation skills, vocabulary, vocal projection, articulation and ability to express themselves. Drama can help students to develop transferable skills, such as problem solving, teamwork, public speaking, leadership and time management.
In today’s complex world, drama at Kew House School gives students the opportunity to explore, discuss and deal with difficult issues, express emotions and explore cultural values.
‘Kew House goes all West End’ Every year we go all out to stage a main school production, usually a musical, which gives a wide range of students a flavour of what it is like to be involved in a professional production, either on stage or behind the scenes, and to showcase their immense talents.
Past productions include: Joseph and the Amazing Technicolour Dream-Coat, Guys ‘n’ Dolls, Pygmalion, Little Shop of Horrors and High Society. ‘Summer Showcase’ At the end of the Summer Term our Year 7s and 8s put on a fabulous event where they present a range of scenes from Shakespeare and other classic plays, interspersed with musical and dance items.
Extra Curricular We offer a rich programme of extra curricular drama, with weekly clubs, allowing students to develop their drama skills and socialise. A Film Club, where pupils can learn about this exciting art form and make their own movies with the opportunity to enter local and national performing arts competitions, such as The English Speaking Union’s ‘Performing Shakespeare Competition’, The Independent Schools Association Drama Festival and Richmond Upon Thames Performing Arts Festival as well as the opportunity to study for LAMDA grades with our specialist teacher
GCSE and A Level Drama Students can opt to study drama at GCSE level from Year 9 and A Level Drama from Year 12. The syllabus allows students to pursue acting and or design options such as set, lighting, costume and puppet design. The course includes both practical and written components where pupils will create their own work and explore the works of others. We are also able to arrange lots of trips to the theatre!

Music
“Music can change the world because it can change people” Bono (Musician)
Music is part of the fabric of Kew House School. When pupils join us in Year 7and through to Year 8, music lessons will form part of their weekly curriculum. The Music department consists of four teachers of curriculum music, an assistant and a team of around twenty visiting instrumental teachers to provide students with expert teaching from a range of specialists. We are proud of our excellent facilities; a music suite housing 12 computers with state of the art software including Sibelius and Cubase, a main teaching room with three additional practice rooms and a wonderful theatre space which we use regularly for concerts and performances.
There is a passion for singing at Kew House School and all children sing regularly in year 7 as a way of developing musicianship, notation reading and to gain an understanding of musical elements.
We give all Year 7 pupils lessons with specialist teachers on violin, clarinet, and trombone, which we call the ‘El Sistema’ programme. During their weekly curriculum lesson, all pupils participate in a 30 minute lesson in a small group for a term, rotating between instruments, as we believe learning an instrument is an important part of music education.
A highlight of the annual school Christmas carol service, is the Year 7 massed choir. This welcomes the new year 7s into the music department and celebrates their first term in the school. We are delighted that this event inspires many students to join the school’s Junior Choir as an extra-curricular activity.
As well as the Junior Choir, the collection of vocal ensembles includes a large Senior Choir which have demonstrated versatility by performing music varying from the Bohemian Rhapsody to Mozart and Rachmaninov. Senior students also come together in smaller groups to form vocal ensembles or perform as soloists.
Weekly Extra-Curricular Groups
We offer a full range of instrumental music lessons in school with visiting music tutors. All lessons take place at lunchtimes or after school between 4-6pm to minimise any disruption to other academic subjects. There are also trips to concerts, workshops, and conferences, and talks from visiting specialists
The GCSE course is designed to inspire. It develops life skills, including critical thinking, aesthetic sensitivity, emotional awareness, self-discipline and self-confidence. Students will develop their musical skills and interests including the ability to make music individually and in groups. To study music at this level, students must be able to perform on an instrument or sing and must be prepared to take lessons in a given instrument or vocal in preparation for the exam. The course is 60% controlled assessment and performance, leaving on 40% of marks awarded in the Summer of Year 11
The A Level course is a continuation and extension of the study that student undertake at GCSE level, where students advance their musical skillset and personal style to become dynamic and expressive musicians.

Careers at Kew House School
A young person’s career preparation is their pathway through learning and work. At Kew House, we are committed to ensuring that every student has access to a well-planned programme of activities, guidance, and support to make informed decisions about their future. Our careers programme supports students throughout their time at school and beyond, helping them prepare for successful transitions into higher education, employment, or further training.
Supporting Student Success
Most of our students choose to study A Levels with the aspiration of progressing to higher education. We are proud of our excellent track record in supporting successful applications to top universities in the UK and abroad, including prestigious Russell Group institutions. Students go on to study a wide variety of subjects, from traditional disciplines such as Law, Medicine, Veterinary Science, History, and Economics, to creative fields like Music Production, Art and Design, Film, and Textiles.
Beyond university, our tailored guidance ensures students are equipped to explore alternative pathways, including apprenticeships, vocational training, and international study. We also collaborate with third-party providers to support international applications, enabling students to pursue opportunities in countries such as the USA, Canada, The Netherlands and Australia.
Careers Programme Overview
We provide comprehensive careers education from Years 7 to 13. Students receive guidance at every stage of their education, ensuring their choices align with their skills, interests, and aspirations. Key components of our careers programme include:

RSE – Relationships and Sex Education
At Kew House School the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) curriculum is delivered within the school’s Individuals in Society (IS) course. Our RSE curriculum is set out in the table below. The IS curriculum is reviewed frequently by the Gardener Award, teachers of the course, and the Senior Leadership Team – often with a consultation phase involving pupils.
We have developed the curriculum in consultation with parents, pupils, and staff, taking into account the age, needs, and feelings of pupils. If pupils ask questions outside the scope of this policy, teachers will respond in an appropriate manner, so that pupils are fully informed and do not have to seek ‘unfiltered’ answers online.
RSE is taught within the personal, social, health, and economic education curriculum (PSHE). Biological aspects of RSE are taught within the Science curriculum, and other aspects are included in Religious Education (RE) aspects of the IS course. The curriculum is delivered by class teachers and augmented by visiting speakers in specialist fields (leading both in-person and virtual sessions), with pupils also receiving stand-alone sex education sessions delivered by a trained health professional.
RSE focuses on giving young people the information they need to help them develop healthy, nurturing relationships of all kinds, including:
These areas of learning are taught within the context of family life, taking care to ensure that there is no stigmatisation of children based on their home circumstances, along with reflecting sensitively that some children may have a different structure of support around them.
The aims of Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) at Kew House School are to:
These aims fit within the context of the ethos of Kew House School to recognise and enhance each child as an individual, with a collective mix of attributes and aptitudes. All in the context of a safe and supportive environment.

Drama
We must all do theatre, to find out who we are and to discover who we could become – Augusto Boal
Taking the stage can be a small step for some and a massive leap for others. At Kew House School, Drama is something we want every pupil to experience, no matter the size of the part. Taking part in a dramatic production either in front of an audience or behind the scenes is a life changing experience – building confidence, developing new skills and achieving a sense of accomplishment.
Drama is a timetabled lesson for Year 7 so that all our students get a taste of this important discipline. Part of their lessons will be devising original work, spoken word as well as performing set pieces. Additionally Drama lessons concentrate on educating our students broader lessons about the craft including textual analysis, technical skills and directing. There are also frequent trips to see West End productions from Shakespeare to musicals.
At Kew House, pupils can opt to study Drama from Year 9. We follow the AQA GSCE Drama syllabus which allows pupils to pursue acting and/or design options such as set, lighting, costume or puppet design. The course offers both practical and written components. Pupils create their own work, explore play-texts and go on LOTS of trips to the theatre.
At A-Level, students also study the AQA syllabus which inspires students to become independent learners with the skills they need to go on to higher education, whether that is to study a course in drama and theatre, or another subject. This qualification emphasises practical creativity alongside research and theoretical understanding. Students learn through experience and will gain many invaluable skills, both theatrical and transferable, to expand their horizons.
Extra-curricular Drama
Kew House offers a rich programme with weekly clubs for Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4 pupils. In these clubs, pupils develop their Drama skills and socialise – it’s serious fun. We also offer a Film Club where pupils can learn about this exciting art form and make their own movies.
Pupils have the opportunity to enter local and national performing arts competitions such as:
In the past we have had great success in these competitions with Kew House pupils taking first place in many categories.
Pupils from Kew House have also taken part in the National Youth Theatre (NYT) and National Youth Music Theatre (NYMT) summer programmes, and several students have successfully auditioned for the Youth Lyric, NYT, and NYMT companies and productions.
Every November we showcase our main school production, usually a musical. These productions give the pupils a flavour of what it’s like to be in a professional production, whether on stage or behind the scenes.
Past productions include:
At the end of the Summer Term, the focus turns to our youngest performers with the annual Year 7 and 8 Summer Showcase. Pupils from these year groups present a range of scenes from Shakespeare and other classic plays, interspersed with musical and dance items.
Students may also study for LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts) grades with our specialist teacher on Mondays and Tuesdays after school. Kew House pupils have maintained a 100% pass rate and several of our senior students have attained their Gold Medal.

Music
Music plays an integral role at Kew House School and is inclusive for all students and abilities
The Music department is a central part of life at Kew House School. All pupils have weekly curriculum lessons in Year 7 and 8 and can then opt for Eduqas GCSE, Eduqas A-level, or BTEC courses. Students also engage with the department by taking part in an array of extra-curricular activities, through individual instrumental lessons, or participating in our concerts as a musician or audience member.
The Music department consists of four teachers of curriculum music, a music assistant, and a team of around twenty visiting instrumental teachers. There is a music suite with 12 computers with software including Sibelius and Cubase and three practice rooms, alongside the main teaching room and the theatre space.
Singing is a particular passion and strength of Kew House School. All children sing regularly in curriculum music lessons in year 7 as a way of developing musicianship, notation reading, and understanding musical elements. A highlight of the annual Christmas carol service, hosted by a local church, is the whole year 7 massed choir accompanied by a small orchestra. This welcomes year 7s into the department and celebrates their first term in the school and inspires many pupils to join the Junior Choir as an extra-curricular activity.
As well as the Junior Choir, the collection of vocal ensembles includes a large Senior Choir which have demonstrated versatility by performing music varying from the Bohemian Rhapsody to Mozart and Rachmaninov. Senior students also come together in smaller groups to form vocal ensembles or perform as soloists.
We are proud to give all Year 7 pupils lessons with specialist teachers on violin, clarinet, and trombone, which we call the ‘El Sistema’ programme. During their weekly curriculum lesson, all pupils participate in a 30 minute lesson in a small group for a term, rotating between instruments, as we believe learning an instrument is an important part of music education. Many pupils choose to continue with one of these instruments in year 8 and beyond by joining one of the junior instrumental ensembles: string ensemble, brass ensemble or woodwind ensemble.
The collection of weekly extra-curricular music groups includes:
We offer a full range of instrumental music lessons in school with visiting music tutors. All lessons take place at lunchtimes or after school between 4-6pm to minimise any disruption to other academic subjects. There are also trips to concerts, workshops, and conferences, and talks from visiting specialists.

Sixth Form Pastoral Care
Sixth Formers have specific pastoral needs and we provide comprehensive, realistic, practical and in-depth pastoral support that enables students to navigate the potential pressures of their later teenage years.
The Personal Tutor’s role is also crucial at this stage. The school is a community where each individual is encouraged to take responsibility for the well-being of the whole. UNIVERSITY ADVISORY – Admission to the best universities and the most demanding courses in the country requires more than high grades alone.
From Year 11 each pupil is assigned a dedicated University Advisor, a specialist in either: a particular subject field, certain type of UK universities or for overseas applications. We guide our students throughout the UCAS process. As a part of the Gardener Schools Group, we can draw on the resources and knowledge of other schools in the group, should we be unable to provide something ourselves.
We also encourage our Sixth Form to take more responsibility for their time and their work management. We reward their growing maturity with more freedom and independence. While still having the safety net of a Personal Tutor who will, in the case of those pupils who joined Kew House School in Year 7, really know the individual Sixth Former.

Art
Art comes from everywhere. It’s your response to your surroundings – Damien Hirst
Art at Kew House School provides students with vast opportunities for cultural, practical and personal exploration and growth. Through the medium of visual communication, Art delves into the depths and nuances of cultural, political, societal and individual reflection, promoting critical thinking and creative problem-solving from research and experimentation to outcome. With state-of-the-art facilities, and experimentation that goes beyond the sketch books, including an open-plan studio and outside-of-school spaces, to equip every creative endeavor and build a competitive portfolio, enabling students to secure places at top art schools.
Being an Art student at Kew House School is a completely immersive experience, with a blended learning practice of specialised teachers, peer learning and group activities. Workshops and visits from professional practitioners, and trips to creative spaces, all allow for a varied and dynamic learning experience.
During Year 7 and 8, Pupil’s progression is nurtured through a combination of technique development and experimentation, coupled with an encouragement for independence of thought, to develop and refine their individual ideas and personal outcomes. Providing the foundations through which original, reflective, critical and quality work will continue and progress at GCSE and A-Level stage.
Course work for GCSE starts in Year 9, consisting of research, experimentation and reflection in an A3 sketchbook. The units then conclude by creating a final piece/controlled assessment in the summer term, deriving from the sketchbook work and exploration from the previous part of the year. Each module will have a topic from which students will apply their creative and critical thinking to explore and present their individual interpretations of said topic.
Students will be exposed to, and discover a range of artists, designers, styles and genres from which they will take inspiration in their own creations. The course requires students to show and identify connections between their references and their own work, demonstrating and articulating the details of the influence.
Experimentation through a variety of mediums and disciplines is highly encouraged to achieve individual and creative excellence. These include (but are not limited to): drawing, painting, sculpture, installation, photography, textile design, printmaking, mixed media, and land art. Throughout which, pupils are supported by highly skilled and dynamic staff in fostering a comprehensive understanding and skill set of artistic disciplines and theory. Students gain essential transferable experience working within real-world frameworks and, when relevant, make connections to creative industries.
Further advancement then takes place at A-Level on the Fine Art Course, where students’ well-developed knowledge, technique and individual style is injected into practices that will further equip them for higher academic and professional progression.

English
“Today a reader, tomorrow a leader”
– Margaret Fuller (Journalist, Editor, Feminist)
At Kew House, we believe studying English is fundamental, and we aim to create a life-long love of literature and language, in all its forms, through reading, writing, speaking, performing and listening. The English curriculum is designed to help students hone and develop their ability to analyse character, theme and structure in a variety of mediums. A key focus at the early stage is understanding how literature has adapted across time and because of societal change. The curriculum also develops students’ ability to create a literary argument though embracing and dissecting their opinions using precise, structured, and engaging writing. This learning is pivotal in forming the desired skills for success at GCSE English Language & Literature.
During GCSE years, the study of English is split into two categories: English Language and English Literature and are examined separately.
English Language GCSE (AQA) asks students to read a range of non-fiction and fiction texts spanning 19th, 20th, and 21st century. The syllabus also draws on ‘unseen’ extracts which encourages pupils to read, write and analyse independently. The writing component of English language requires students to write with specificity; they may be asked to write a diary entry, review, or an advertisement. At Kew House School we focus on developing students’ ability to write with a critical eye to evolve their understanding of different styles of writing. The language course also emphasises proper grammar, vocabulary, and spelling. Final assessments take the form of two separate examinations.
The English language is nobody’s special property. It is the property of the imagination; it is the property of the language itself.”
– Sir Derek Walcott Nobel Prize for Literature 1992, Poet and Playwright)
The GCSE English Literature course has three strands: play, poetry and novel. Specifically, students will study a 19th century novel, a Shakespeare play, and a series of poems dated from the 19th-21st centuries. Students also study an additional British novel or play from 1914 onwards. In previous years texts included: William Shakespeare’s Macbeth, A Christmas Carol by Charles Dickens, An Inspector Calls by J.B Presley and a Power and Conflict poetry collection by an assortment of poets. There are two English Literature examinations, both of which are closed book, meaning pupils are not provided with a copy of any of the texts during examinations. Students will learn how to compare two unseen extracts together, synthesising their similarities and differences to create a succinct and well-developed argument.

History
We are not makers of history. We are made by history.
Martin Luther King, Jr.
The department teaches in a suite of 3 rooms in the main building and specialist Sixth Form rooms at Pier House. All spaces are equipped with interactive white boards and audio-visual facilities.
We follow a programme of study covering history from the Norman Conquest to Civil Rights in America. The key focus is the role of individuals and how they shaped Britain and the wider world.
We follow the OCR Schools History Project specification covering Crime and Punishment c1250-Present Day, The Elizabethans 1580-1603, The making of America 1789-1900, Living under the Nazis 1933-1945 and History Around Us which is a site study.
We follow the OCR specification studying The Early Stuarts and the Origins of the Civil War 1603–1660, International Relations 1890–1941 and Russia and its Rulers 1855–1964. There is also a coursework unit, the focus of which is decided by the student.
Click here to learn more about the sixth form.
Co-curricular Activities
The department offers a range of activities to engage pupils in the lower school such as competitions, essay and creative writing tasks. At GCSE and A level, students are provided with activities, lectures and opportunities that will provide them with an excellent foundation for those wishing to study history at university or who are preparing for Oxbridge entry.
Super Curricular Sixth Form 2026
In the lower school, pupils will make local visits and in recent years this has included Hampton Court, Kensington Palace and the Clink Museum.
At GCSE, pupils will visit Greenwich Park as part of the ‘History Around Us’ unit and other sites such as the Imperial War Museum and the London Dungeons.
In addition, the department runs international trips for Year 8,9 and Sixth Form to the battlefields of the First or Second World War. In recent years this has included Gallipoli-Turkey, the Somme and Ypres, Normandy and more recently Thessaloniki- Greece. Kew House School were the first school in the UK to take pupils for a First World War battlefields trip to the region.
In Year 10 the pupils have the opportunity to visit Germany or Poland as part of their GCSE study of ‘Living under the Nazis’ and in recent years this has included Munich and Nuremberg, Berlin and Krakow.
In recent years students have gone on to read History or related courses at Oxford, Cambridge, Durham, Manchester and Bristol amongst other universities.
